result:
The two greatest unattainable scores are 39 and 31, so their product is 1209.

A score n is attainable exactly when n = 8a + 9b + 19c for nonnegative integers a, b, c. Since 8 is available, n is attainable if and only if n is at least the smallest attainable value with the same residue mod 8. Using 9 ≡ 1 and 19 ≡ 3 (mod 8), the smallest attainable value for each residue is:

| Residue mod 8 | Smallest attainable | Representation |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 9 | 9 |
| 2 | 18 | 9·2 |
| 3 | 19 | 19 |
| 4 | 28 | 19 + 9 |
| 5 | 37 | 19 + 2·9 |
| 6 | 38 | 2·19 |
| 7 | 47 | 2·19 + 9 |

The unattainable scores are the numbers n ≡ r (mod 8) with n below the smallest attainable value for r. The largest of these thresholds is 47 (residue 7), so the Frobenius number is 47 − 8 = 39. Every integer from 40 to 47 is attainable, and adding 8 keeps everything beyond attainable, so 39 is the largest unattainable score.

The next largest candidate is in residue class 7, which gives 31 (since 31 < 47). Checking 31 directly: 31 − 9b − 19c must be a nonnegative multiple of 8 with c ≤ 1, and no choice of b and c works. So 31 is unattainable. Every number from 32 to 38 is attainable (for example 38 = 2·19, 37 = 19 + 18, 36 = 28 + 8, 35 = 19 + 16, 34 = 18 + 16, 33 = 9 + 24, 32 = 8·4), so 31 is the second largest unattainable score.

The product is 39 × 31 = 1209.

ANSWER: 1209
